decisions.why: 'Only an applied transaction consumes the sequence' (kept from the old golden) reads as if a failed transaction does not consume it. A transaction included in a ledger consumes its sequence and fee even when its operations fail; only one rejected before inclusion does not. Make that explicit and split the replacement fact.

evidence.quote: For each transaction, the account's sequence number is consumed (increased by 1), the transaction's validity is rechecked, and each operation is applied... Operations may fail at this stage
If the transaction is invalid, it will be rejected immediately by Stellar Core, the account's sequence number will not be incremented, and no fee will be consumed
it's valid when S satisfies minSeqNum <= S < tx.seqNum ... after a transaction is executed, the account will always set its sequence number to the transaction's sequence number.

finalRewrite.answer: Sequence numbers are per source account, with no global order across accounts. By default a transaction needs current sequence + 1, so N+2 at N fails tx_bad_seq. CAP-0021 minSeqNum is the exception: it is valid when minSeqNum <= current < transaction sequence, then advances the account to that sequence. A transaction included in a ledger consumes its sequence even if its operations fail; one rejected at submission does not. A queued same-source, same-sequence transaction can be replaced by a fee-bump bidding 10x.
keyFacts: Sequence is per source account; the default is exactly current + 1.
CAP-0021 minSeqNum can permit a gap and advance the sequence directly.
An included transaction consumes its sequence even if it fails; a rejected one does not.
A queued transaction can be replaced by a fee-bump bidding at least 10x.
avoid: Do NOT say N+2 can never apply, or that a transaction rejected before inclusion consumes sequence.
finalRewrite.notes: Grade queue replacement separately from preconditions; behavior depends on the submission path.
